27 The siren of a moving police car emits a sound wave with a frequency of 440 Hz. A stationary
observer hears sound of frequency 494 Hz. The speed of sound in the air is 340 m s–1.
What could be the speed and the direction of movement of the car?
A
37 m s–1 directly away from the observer
B
37 m s–1 directly towards the observer
C
42 m s–1 directly away from the observer
D
42 m s–1 directly towards the observer

hints: Compare $440 \text{ Hz}$ emitted with $494 \text{ Hz}$ heard: an increase in frequency means the wavefronts are bunched up by motion towards the stationary observer.
Recall the moving-source Doppler equation $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ for approach, where $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the speed of sound.
Rearrange to $v - v_s = v(f_s/f_o)$, substitute $440/494$, then solve for $v_s$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and check whether $37$ or $42$ fits.
walkthrough: Observed frequency $494 \text{ Hz}$ is greater than source frequency $440 \text{ Hz}$. For sound, higher frequency means shorter observed wavelength, which happens when the source moves directly towards the stationary observer.
Use the Doppler effect for an approaching source: $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$, where $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $f_s = 440 \text{ Hz}$ and $f_o = 494 \text{ Hz}$.
Rearrange for the source speed: $v - v_s = v \times f_s/f_o$, so $v_s = v - v \times f_s/f_o$.
Substitute values: $v_s = 340 - 340 \times 440/494$. Since $340/494 \approx 0.688$, then $340 \times 440/494 \approx 303 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Hence $v_s \approx 340 - 303 \approx 37 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The unit remains $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and the value matches the lower speed, not $42 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
A speed of about $37 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ directly towards the observer gives the observed increase. This is option B.

A.explanation: Observed $494 \text{ Hz}$ is higher than emitted $440 \text{ Hz}$, so wavelength is shortened and the car cannot be moving away.

B.explanation: Higher observed frequency means approach, and $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s)$ gives $v_s$ about $37 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards the observer.

C.explanation: Moving away would lower the observed frequency below $440 \text{ Hz}$, not raise it to $494 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: Direction towards is correct for increased frequency, but $42 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives too large a shift, about $517 \text{ Hz}$.
